clue.text: Chap by turns meeting deep dis appointment

definitions.note: the page splits disappointment across a line break

parts.note: bod is British slang for a person or chap

indicators.note: by turns says the little word by is flipped round

parts.note: taken as written before turning
a deep voice is a low one

explanation.surface: A man taking turns while meeting a heavy letdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' makes YB from BY. The newspaper hyphenated 'disappointment' at a line end, which the OCR kept as two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A body blow is figuratively a severe setback, a crushing letdown.

clue.text: Bold extremists holding gun? Quite the opposite

indicators.note: holding would put the gun inside the extremes; the next phrase flips which piece holds which
Quite the opposite reverses the stated container, so the gun word holds the extremes

parts.note: the Bren is a British light machine gun
A and Z are the extremes of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Daring extremists carrying weapons, or the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as written, the extremes would hold the gun; 'Quite the opposite' swaps container and contents.
explanation.definitionFit: Brazen means shamelessly bold, impudent without embarrassment.

clue.text: Periodical presented with covers missing? That takes the biscuit

parts.note: a digest is a magazine summarising news

indicators.note: covers missing says the outer letters of the gift word are dropped

parts.note: presented means given

explanation.surface: A magazine handed over without its covers: that really takes the biscuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covers missing' strips GIVEN to IVE. 'That takes the biscuit' sounds like outrage but points to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A digestive is a British semi-sweet wholemeal biscuit, a favourite with tea.

clue.text: Attack 10's purpose?

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer into BAR RAGE, the goal of 10 across.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrage is a concentrated artillery bombardment, and read as two words, the aim of stopping fury.

clue.text: Indian summer's beginning: love having time outside

indicators.note: having joins outside to say the zero and the era are around the letter
outside says the love and time pieces sit on both sides of that letter

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
an age is a period of time

indicators.note: beginning means take just the first letter of summer's

explanation.surface: An Indian summer starting, with romance enduring over time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian summer' reads as one phrase, but 'Indian' is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: The Osage are a Native American people of the Great Plains, once called Indians.

clue.text: Star Liverpool player wears it?

definitions.meaning: the Daily Star, a British tabloid newspaper of the kind whose masthead is red
Liverpool FC play in red shirts

explanation.surface: A star footballer at Liverpool and the shirt he wears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' looks like a famous player but is the newspaper: a red-top is a British popular tabloid such as the Sun, Mirror or Star.
explanation.definitionFit: Red-top is the British name for a downmarket tabloid, from its red masthead, and also literally a red shirt.

clue.text: Why sea becomes turbulent after middle of September? Nonsense

indicators.note: after puts the scrambled letters behind the central letter
middle of picks the central letter of the nine-letter month
turbulent water churns, so the letters of why and sea are stirred up

explanation.surface: Wondering why the sea turns rough in mid-September.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle (fifth) letter of SEPTEMBER is E, and 'becomes turbulent' turns WHY SEA into YEWASH.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyewash is informal for rubbish or humbug, talk meant to deceive.

clue.text: Specified individuals in. England's most affluent area?

definitions.meaning: people or things pointed out nearby
the South East, read as two words

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer into THE SE, the South East of England, its wealthiest region.
explanation.definitionFit: These points out particular people, and split up names the prosperous English region around London.

clue.text: Numbers on first part of this old recording recalled former pianist

indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, so the whole string runs backwards

parts.note: re means on or concerning

indicators.note: first part of takes the opening letter of this

parts.note: an EP, extended play, is an old record format

explanation.surface: A former pianist remembered through numbers on the start of an old record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns NOSRETEP round. Oscar Peterson was a Canadian jazz pianist who died in 2007.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscar Peterson was a celebrated jazz pianist, now dead, so a pianist of the past.

clue.text: Traveller with a visa finally boarding ferry to travel

indicators.note: boarding puts the visa's final letter aboard the shuffled boat word
to travel says the letters move about into a new order
finally takes the last letter of visa

explanation.surface: A tourist with a visa getting on a ferry for a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with a' gives two pieces, not a link; 'to travel' shuffles the boat word to YFRER before the visa's last letter boards it.
explanation.definitionFit: A wayfarer is a journeyer, especially one going on foot.

clue.text: Self-control needed as yours. truly's taken in by a northern — European spy

parts.note: a German is one kind of European

indicators.note: taken in by says the speaker's pronoun goes inside the longer string that follows

parts.note: a spy is an agent
yours truly is the writer referring to himself, me

explanation.surface: Keeping calm is needed when the writer is fooled by a German spy from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European spy' gives two pieces, and the inserted pronoun lands inside the second, not between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Anger management is therapy for controlling one's temper, a form of self-restraint.

clue.text: Fellow not initially abandoning position on Europe

indicators.note: on puts the second piece after the first in this across answer

parts.note: EU is the European Union

indicators.note: abandoning says a letter is dropped from the position word

parts.note: a stance is a position or attitude

indicators.note: initially says take only the first letter of not

explanation.surface: A man giving up his stance on Europe, with a hint of hesitation.
explanation.walkthrough: N, the first letter of 'not', leaves STANCE to give STACE.
explanation.definitionFit: Eustace is a man's first name, and in crosswords any male name can be clued as a chap or fellow.

clue.text: I stroll about in road wearing warm coat

indicators.note: wearing says the road word is clothed by the coat word around it

parts.note: a fur is a warm coat
a lane is a small road

explanation.surface: Someone ambling along a road in a warm coat.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks as the answer: a stroller describing himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A flaneur is an idle man-about-town who saunters through city streets watching life.

clue.text: In one view, correct to give temporary help

parts.note: read the answer as an instruction: the word tide turned over spells edit, which means correct

explanation.surface: Putting someone right, from one point of view, as a way of helping out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In one view' tells you to look at the answer a second way: as wordplay, TIDE OVER means TIDE turned round, which is EDIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To tide someone over is to see them through a lean spell with a stopgap loan or aid.

clue.text: Absorbing holy scriptures changes them?

indicators.note: Absorbing says the scripture letters are taken inside the word for changes

parts.note: varies means changes
OT is the Old Testament

explanation.surface: Taking in sacred texts transforms the people who study them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'them' points to the answer: devotees changed by reading scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: Votaries are devoted followers, people vowed to religious service.

clue.text: Greeting drunk who wants same again

indicators.note: drunk says the little word who staggers into a new order

parts.note: do is short for ditto, meaning the same again

explanation.surface: A tipsy greeter asking for the same drink again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges WHO to HOW. DO, from ditto, is the mark that repeats what is above.
explanation.definitionFit: How do you do is a formal hello, shortened to the hearty how-do.

clue.text: Wife and husband join another couple and tuck into chicken perhaps

parts.note: an item is a couple in a relationship
to tuck into is to eat heartily

explanation.surface: Two couples sitting down together for a roast chicken dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'join' is just the link; 'another couple' means a second pair, an ITEM.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken breast is the classic pale flesh of poultry, as opposed to red meat.

clue.text: City in Pakistan bulldozed, though not entirely

indicators.note: though not entirely says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A city in Pakistan partly flattened by bulldozers.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sets the city in Pakistan, but it is in Turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Istanbul is Turkey's largest city, the former Constantinople.

clue.text: Removes clothing, retiring for this

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the word for undressing is read from its end

parts.note: to peel is to strip off clothes

explanation.surface: Getting undressed and going to bed for a night's rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' turns PEELS round, and doubles as going to bed, which is what you undress for.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue describes getting ready for bed in order to rest through the night.

clue.text: Old man and I move fast in racing boat

parts.note: pa is a father, someone's old man
to roar along is to move at speed

explanation.surface: Father and I speeding along in a rowing boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair-oar is a rowing boat for two rowers, each with one oar, used in racing.

clue.text: Creature quietly digging into ground

indicators.note: digging into says the quiet letter burrows inside the ground word

parts.note: terrain is ground or land
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: An animal burrowing silently into the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrapin is a freshwater turtle, a reptile and so a creature.

clue.text: 20 is taking a couple of pints out of river, just above freezing point?

definitions.note: 20 across is a terrapin, and the clue says it is this: living in water, an adjective

indicators.note: out of says the river letter is taken from the quart

parts.note: a quart is two pints
1C, one degree Celsius, is just above water's freezing point

explanation.surface: A terrapin drinking two pints from the river in near-freezing weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' removes R from QUART to give QUAT. The 1 of 1C is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrapin is a turtle living in fresh water, so it is a water-dwelling creature.

clue.text: Ibsen heroine, we hear, is a brick .'

parts.note: Hedda Gabler is the heroine of Ibsen's play

clue.text: Unreliable report on software that's right for job-seeker?

indicators.note: on places the report word after the software word in this across answer

parts.note: an app is a piece of software
a lie is an untrue account

clue.text: Seedy district in Derbyshire described thus?

definitions.meaning: seedy means slightly unwell or off-colour
the Peak District in Derbyshire, with an adjective ending

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition makes an adjective from the Peak District, the hill country of Derbyshire in northern England.

clue.text: Sandwich lover?

clue.text: Very good day for broadcast

parts.note: so! is an interjection meaning very well, that's right, as in so be it

explanation.definitionFit: To broadcast seed is to scatter it widely by hand, which is how it was sown.

clue.text: After defeat, is tense and down, suffering despair

clue.text: Shoots fowl?

clue.text: Teacher's the reverse of discourteous about Roman censor

definitions.note: the 's is short for is, linking the definition to the rest

indicators.note: about says the turned word goes around the censor's name
the reverse of says the impolite word is read backwards
